questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Availability of transgender healthcare, cultural values

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing was a struggle

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy on my own, I got help from the SSC

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received some help from the SSC in finding available housing, after one week of unreliable or victimizing airbnb hosts

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I felt very stressed and "on my own" from the initial week until semester start. I realize I probably should have applied to welcome week, but felt I had too much on my plate with trying to figure out housing and medicine

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very hard to find housing.
Most posted online at an affordable range were discriminating by sex and did not feel trans/queer inclusive.
My first airbnb place was falling apart and in a terrible neighborhood, at the second i was harassed by the owner.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The housing situation is tough. Find a place in advance. It will be pricey

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I find it irresponsible to take in many more students when dorms are full in this housing market. Please do more to assure the student you invite into your country and university have secure housing during their entire stay

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Please let your exchange student talk to you before they arrive.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
- get approval for the courses you want to sign up for with administration
- fit everything into a schedule in mosaic
- repeat steps when the courses get filled during the process...

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Little to no help was available before entering Canada. 
After, it is easier to get ahold of administration or counseling, but the setbacks I encountered still stopped me from getting the courses I wanted

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unsuccessful. The process of getting waived for courses and applying was longer than it took for all my first and second choices to get filled. I ended up with two of my four classes at a low level with repetitious material to classes i've already taken at home

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Honestly it's a mess. Try to get your letter of admission, mosaic login, and get your course permissions with admin before arriving. When your emails don't get answered, find more adresses to email.
It's much easier when you're in the country, but you won't get courses you want if they are popular

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level varied widely.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was less reliant on and trusting of students independently engaging with class. Much more of the schedule was "mandatory", and more students in lectures were disengaged or outright disruptive.
This was mostly in the lower-level courses. Some professors had a more familiar and, in my opinion, effective teaching style

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
2C03
2LC3
3MI3
4ML3

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend 4ML3 (intro to machine learning). An interesting topic with its bases explained thoroughly. Best if you have taken linear algebra before

questions.answer: Try to get some fresh air, try the hiking trails, meet new people.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is somewhat of a taboo against "calling out" anything wrong in favor of passiveness.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: General acceptance of trans and other lgbt+ folks.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- figure out housing asap
- advocate for yourself
- don't be afraid of talking to people, most will appreciate it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: downtown Hamilton is a bad place to live. try to find something in Westdale

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing
